hypothesis_text: Altcoins exhibiting extreme idiosyncratic 4-hour return divergence relative to Bitcoin (|return_4h_btc_neutral| > 0.012) suffer from temporary liquidity dislocation and inventory overextension. When conditioned on extreme aggressive order flow (taker_buy_ratio_1h) and orderbook resting depth asymmetry (depth_imbalance_10), these idiosyncratic shocks mean-revert over 1h to 4h forward horizons as aggressive momentum chasers exhaust liquidity and passive market makers restore cross-sectional parity.
narrative: In crypto perpetual futures, price moves often bifurcate into market-wide systematic moves (driven by Bitcoin) and idiosyncratic token-specific moves. Over a 4-hour lookback, an altcoin moving independently of BTC by more than 1.2% represents substantial idiosyncratic capital allocation. When this move is driven by aggressive takers consuming top-of-book depth, short-term momentum chasers and levered retail participants rush into the move, creating an inventory imbalance for liquidity providers. As the initial aggressive order flow subsides, market makers widen spreads and adjust quotes to rebalance inventory, forcing late chasers to exit at unfavorable prices. Simultaneously, cross-sectional arbitrageurs sell overextended outperformers and buy underperformers against BTC to capture spread mean-reversion. Conditioning on taker flow (taker_buy_ratio_1h) identifies the moments where aggressive liquidity consumption reaches climactic levels, while conditioning on depth imbalance (depth_imbalance_10) measures resting absorption capacity that halts further price extension.
research_rationale:
The anchor signal XL_SOLUSDT_0b1e2e14afb8 is locked from expression_lab on SOLUSDT over the 15m scan panel (2024-06-01 to 2025-08-04) with expression abs(return_4h_btc_neutral) > 0.012, matching 8,143 bars on SOLUSDT (20.74% match rate, 384 independent events) and 26,028 rows pooled across majors (16.57% match rate, 406 independent days). The distribution of return_4h_btc_neutral is symmetric (mean -0.000028, std 0.0103, 12,950 positive vs 13,078 negative bars on the panel), with 4h autocorrelation dropping to -0.0095, confirming that shocks are non-persistent beyond the 4h formation window.

In inspect_catalog.cemetery, the dominant historical kill code for return_4h_btc_neutral was T0.04-IC-STAT (245 trials), demonstrating that unconditional, dense formulas lack sufficient signal-to-noise ratio and trade too frequently. Furthermore, T1.20-REGIME-FILTER (61 trials) and T1.10-ICIR (55 trials) indicate that arbitrary regime masks degrade stability. To address these failure modes: (1) we employ a locked predicate (abs > 0.012) creating event-driven execution that eliminates low-conviction noise bars; (2) we avoid fragile masked regimes by testing at target_regime 'all'; (3) we focus on 1h and 2h horizons, where cemetery survival was highest (14.4% and 9.2%, vs 4.3% at 4h).

For composition_plan, inspect_catalog.gene_knowledge priors identify taker_buy_ratio_1h as the primary trigger partner (n=60, confidence sufficient, shrink_weight 0.75, recommending opposite-side / extreme flow gating for cross-sectional rotation reversal). We include gate_high, gate_low, and gate_tail on taker_buy_ratio_1h to capture climactic buying and selling exhaustion. In addition, orderbook depth imbalance (depth_imbalance_10) is introduced as an absorption partner, consistent with cemetery trials where depth_imbalance_10 spread/gate combinations achieved positive T1 survival (15.2%). Both partners achieved 1.0 coverage in probe_partner with projected T1 event observations well exceeding the 250-observation threshold. Full search scope is chosen to explore automatic grid pairings while prioritizing the authored event-gated seeds.
